card: Adds an -ipcconnect option to bitcoin-gui in multiprocess builds, allowing the GUI to connect over IPC to an already-running bitcoin-node daemon instead of spawning a new node subprocess. By default (-ipcconnect=auto), the GUI checks for a socket at sockets/node.sock and connects if available, falling back to spawning a node if not. This allows users of experimental multiprocess builds to start and stop GUI instances independently of the background node. The PR is part of the process separation project (#28722) and is stacked on #10102, #19460, and #29409, containing only a single unique commit.
changed_since_previous: Rebased on updated versions of the base stack (#10102, #19460, #29409), incorporating upstream libmultiprocess subtree merges and btcsignals callback destruction updates, while leaving the final commit unchanged.
evidence: PR description: 'This allows the GUI to be started and stopped independently of the node. By default with this change, bitcoin-gui will check if a <datadir>/sockets/node.sock socket exists and try to connect to that. If that doesn't work, it will spawn a new node process and start up the same way it did before this PR.'
PR description: 'Part of the process separation project (issue #28722)'
problem: In multiprocess builds, `bitcoin-gui` automatically spawns and owns its own `bitcoin-node` subprocess that shuts down when the GUI closes. Users cannot keep a long-running background node daemon and attach or detach GUI instances independently.

risk.why: Mistakes in IPC socket connection or initialization could cause GUI startup failures, unhandled exceptions during disconnection, or silent ignoring of node configuration options.

scope_notes: This PR is stacked on #10102, #19460, and #29409. Only the single top commit (b6e97e431a) is unique to this PR; the remaining 27 commits and bulk of the +4419/-662 diff belong to the underlying stack and libmultiprocess subtree updates.
summary: Adds an `-ipcconnect` command-line option to `bitcoin-gui` for multiprocess builds, enabling it to connect to an existing `bitcoin-node` process over IPC instead of spawning a new child process. By default (`-ipcconnect=auto`), it attempts to connect to `<datadir>/sockets/node.sock` if present and falls back to spawning a dedicated node process.
